newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Apr 28.

text.p: There are 64 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the low-profile approach taken by Chinese officials at the opening ceremony for Hong Kong's Tsing Ma Bridge showed Beijing might not send senior leaders to the territory's handover ceremony on June 30. It said the bridge was built as part of measures taken by Britain to boost local confidence after the crushing of pro-democracy protests in Beijing in 1989, but the efforts were not appreciated by China.

-- The MING PAO DAILY said the British government had left Hong Kong a precious legacy, including an independent judicial system, clean administrative body, fair commercial environment and a free lifestyle.

-- The Beijing-backed TA KUNG PAO said that both blue chips and red chips were important in stabilising the Hong Kong stock market, and Chinese companies did not enjoy higher status in Hong Kong. The paper said it was time to accelerate the process of including some red-chip shares in the Hang Seng Index.

-- The English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST said it would make sense for Hong Kong to play a greater role in screening immigrant applications from the mainland. It said the territory must uphold the rule of law and that laws could not be ignored to suit administrative expediency.
